facts.statement: The study compared 42 people with spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 to 17 healthy controls.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants were split into groups based on ataxia severity and cognitive status, with 12 having mild ataxia and 30 having moderate-to-severe ataxia.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: People with the condition showed difficulties with executive function, visual working memory, and spatial planning compared to the control group.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Those with more severe ataxia had worse visual working memory and task accuracy than those with mild ataxia.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Patients with intact cognition took longer to process information, while only those with cognitive impairment had issues with delayed responses.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Specific cerebellar regions were linked to different cognitive abilities, such as spatial planning and visual working memory.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study concludes that the cognitive problems in this condition are linked to changes in specific parts of the cerebellum.
facts.subject: humans
